text: I think the question of mech vs membrane is so hyped up to some extent. I think what mech keyboards give you is just slightly better tactile, better tactile and better precision. For writer, programmer, gamer, it's really very satisfying. And the longevity is pretty good. You can swap out the keycaps, switch. You can tinker around and repair. It's very customisable. You can program it, you can hot swap it. So it's very personal and more sustainable and better for your wallet in a long run. But that doesn't necessarily mean that it's better. There's a lot of trade-offs involved. They can be very expensive. They can be very loud. They can be very annoying to your family or your colleague. So if you're working in an office with other people, noise becomes a bigger concern than tactile. And the number of hours that you would spend to choose the right switch, right layout, right keycap, etc. And then the gimmicky thing is that people just keep buying switches, buying keycaps, buying new stuff. So it can become very very expensive. But also, a mechanical keyboard doesn't necessarily guarantee faster typing, better ergonomics, better posture, better productivity. If you have bad posture, then it's just going to hurt regardless of the keyboard. And in terms of ergonomics and tactile, some people are just comfortable with membrane keyboards. So yeah, I would say that it's not a necessary. But it's a very good investment, if you really care about tactile, customisation and longevity. Just that, choose a right keyboard that fits your needs.
